value.s10: Half a chicken roasted over the embers, with leeks, crushed potatoes and a rosemary gravy.
value.s20: Half a corn fed chicken, roasted over the embers in the dining room until the skin is smoky and crisp. It comes with soft leeks, crushed potatoes and a gravy made from the roasting juices and rosemary.
value.s45: This is the dish the room opened on. Half a corn fed chicken goes over the embers of the hearth you can see from the door, and roasts until the skin is smoky and crisp and the meat is still juicy. It rests, then it is carved at the pass and set on soft leeks and crushed potatoes, with a gravy made from the roasting juices, a little rosemary and a squeeze of lemon. It is a plate for one, and the regulars order it without looking at the card.

value.sayIt: With the chicken I would pour the Harbour White. It is dry and bright, and it loves the smoke.

value.s10: A dry white from the slope above the harbour, crisp, with a salty finish.
value.s20: This is Bacchus from Quay Lane, grown on the chalk above the harbour and fermented cool in steel. It is dry and bright, green apple and cut grass, with a salty finish that suits the chicken.
value.s45: The Harbour White is the one wine on the list you can see the vines of from the window. Quay Lane planted Bacchus on the chalk slope above the harbour and this is the third vintage. It is fermented cool in steel with no oak, so what you get is the grape: green apple, cut grass and a long salty finish from the sea air. It is the first pick with the roast chicken, because the acid cuts the skin and the salt meets the gravy, and it is nine by the glass or thirty eight the bottle.

why.value: The rosemary is the same sprig that goes into the gravy, so the bar and the kitchen taste of one room.

pairs.value: Before the chicken, or with the beetroot salad.

origin.value: A Collins is a long gin drink from the old London hotel bars; this one took the house rosemary.

value.technique: Built over cubed ice and stirred, topped with soda

value.s10: A long gin drink with lemon, rosemary syrup and soda, built over ice.
value.s20: The Lantern Collins is our long drink: gin, fresh lemon and a rosemary syrup we make from the sprigs the kitchen uses, built over cubed ice and topped with soda. Sharp, long, and the rosemary comes through on the finish.
value.s45: The Lantern Collins is the house long drink. A Collins is an old London hotel bar drink, gin lengthened with citrus and soda, and ours takes the rosemary that goes into the roast chicken gravy, made into a syrup at the bar. Fifty of gin, a good squeeze of lemon, the syrup, built over cubed ice in a highball and topped with soda, with a sprig on top. It is sharp and long and it drinks well before the chicken or beside the beetroot salad.
